name: ADRA Recovery Passport Foundational Knowledge Base
description: Embedded Cost Recovery design, Master Time Schedule operational design, workbook formula catalog and unified work-evidence integration knowledge used to ground the system agent.

records.title: Cost Recovery knowledge 1
records.content: Its core concepts—timesheets, payroll allocation, eligibility checks, approval workflow, and anomaly detection—already exist separately. The opportunity is to combine them into something unusually simple and defensible.

records.title: How the prototype currently ranks
records.content:
How the prototype currently ranks
Area | Current position
Actual-time allocation | Strong
Expected-hours denominator | Strong and safer than the old workbook
Payroll reconciliation | Strong concept; benefits still need configuration
Donor eligibility | Designed but using provisional information
Exception management | Strong prototype
AI assistance | Simulated, not connected to an AI service
Audit trail | Workbook-level only
Electronic approvals | Not yet implemented
Security and access control | Not yet production-ready
Accounting-system integration | Not yet implemented
Global uniqueness | Cannot be established
The prototype already aligns with an important international principle: personnel charges should reflect work actually performed and be supported by internal controls giving reasonable assurance that costs are accurate, allowable, and properly allocated. 2 CFR 200.430 also expects salary distribution across activities when employees work on multiple cost objectives.
This matters because USAID audit work has identified recurring problems involving fixed percentage allocations, incomplete recording of an employee’s total activities, and time charged differently from actual work performed. USAID OIG audit example

records.title: A simpler gold-standard concept
records.content:
A simpler gold-standard concept
I recommend redesigning the final system around one idea:

records.title: The Recovery Passport
records.content:
The Recovery Passport
Every proposed personnel charge receives a small digital “passport” containing five keys.
Key | Question | Result
Evidence | Was the work recorded and approved? | Pass/Fail
Capacity | Does total time reconcile to expected time? | Pass/Fail
Eligibility | Was the employee allowed to work on this project? | Pass/Fail
Budget | Is the cost allowable and within the available budget? | Pass/Fail
Approval | Have the employee, supervisor, and finance approved it? | Pass/Fail

records.title: Cost Recovery knowledge 5
records.content:
The accounting formula becomes exceptionally simple:
Recoverable Cost
= Approved Hours
× Employment Hourly Cost
× Recovery Gate
Where:
Recovery Gate
=EvidenceKey

records.title: Cost Recovery knowledge 6
records.content:
*CapacityKey
*EligibilityKey
*BudgetKey
*ApprovalKey
Each key is either 1 or 0.
Therefore:
All five pass: cost is recoverable.
One fails: posting is blocked.

records.title: Cost Recovery knowledge 7
records.content:
The system explains exactly why.
The underlying cost remains visible and is never lost.
The readiness score remains useful for management, but it does not authorize accounting.

records.title: What employees would see
records.content:
What employees would see
The employee should see only one simple screen:
Date | What did you do? | Hours | Suggested Project
1 Aug | Reviewed partner financial report | 2.0 | FOSTER — 94%
1 Aug | Country management meeting | 6.0 | ADMIN — 91%

records.title: Cost Recovery knowledge 9
records.content:
The employee accepts or changes the suggestion.
They should not see:
Payroll rates
Donor budget calculations
Cost-allocation formulas
Complex voucher schedules

records.title: What supervisors would see
records.content:
What supervisors would see
Supervisors should see only exceptions:
Missing six hours
Weekend work without an explanation
Unusual project selection
Project outside its active period
Activity inconsistent with the chosen project
Material change from normal working patterns

records.title: Cost Recovery knowledge 11
records.content: This is “management by exception.” Supervisors do not need to inspect every formula or every compliant entry.

records.title: What finance would see
records.content:
What finance would see
Finance should receive an automatically generated Recovery Passport:
Field | Example
Employee | John Mwanza
Month | June 2026
Project | ASPIRE
Approved hours | 33
Expected monthly hours | 160
Allocable employment cost | UGX 10,450,000
Hourly cost | UGX 65,312.50
Proposed charge | UGX 2,155,312.50
Evidence | Pass
Capacity | Fail—six hours missing
Eligibility | Pass
Budget | Pass
Approval | Pass
Final status | Blocked

records.title: Cost Recovery knowledge 13
records.content: Finance immediately knows the amount, evidence, and reason for blocking.

records.title: The genuinely innovative combination
records.content:
The genuinely innovative combination
The potential innovation is not merely “AI in a timesheet.” That is increasingly common. The distinctive design would combine four capabilities.

records.title: 1. Evidence-to-charge traceability
records.content:
1. Evidence-to-charge traceability
Every voucher amount can be traced:
Voucher
→ employee cost
→ approved hours
→ daily activity
→ human approval
→ donor rule

records.title: Cost Recovery knowledge 16
records.content:
→ payroll record
No unexplained aggregate percentage.

records.title: 2. Counterfactual recovery advice
records.content:
2. Counterfactual recovery advice
When a charge is blocked, the system explains:
Why it is blocked
How much is at risk
Who must act
What action would make it recoverable
Example:
Ugx391,875 remains unsupported because six expected hours are missing. John Mwanza must complete the missing entries, after which the supervisor must reapprove June.

records.title: Cost Recovery knowledge 18
records.content: This makes the tool a recovery assistant, not merely a calculator.

records.title: 3. AI with a restricted role
records.content:
3. AI with a restricted role
AI may:
Suggest projects
Classify activities
Explain exceptions
Detect unusual patterns
Draft follow-up reminders
Summarize recovery risks

records.title: Cost Recovery knowledge 20
records.content:
AI may not:
Change hours
Approve time
Determine salary
Override donor restrictions
Authorize journal entries
That boundary makes the design practical and auditable.

records.title: 4. Learning from approved decisions
records.content:
4. Learning from approved decisions
When an employee repeatedly accepts the same coding:
“Partner financial review” → FOSTER → Financial monitoring
the system learns the pattern. However, it continues showing the suggestion and confidence rather than silently posting it.

records.title: The ideal three-screen system
records.content:
The ideal three-screen system
To remain simple, the final application should have only three operational screens:
My Time — employee records activities and accepts AI suggestions.
Exceptions — supervisor and finance resolve blocked items.
Recovery Voucher — finance reviews and posts approved charges.
Employee, project, payroll, calendar, and donor-rule masters remain behind these screens as controlled administration areas.

records.title: What would make it a gold standard
records.content:
What would make it a gold standard
The production version should eventually include:
Full payroll reconciliation
Configurable donor rules
Project-budget integration
Role-based access
Electronic approval timestamps
Version history

records.title: Cost Recovery knowledge 24
records.content:
Prevention of retrospective unauthorized changes
Complete activity coverage
Automatic accounting-journal output
Supporting-document references
Data privacy controls
Exception notifications
Recovery-risk forecasting
Independent audit testing

records.title: Cost Recovery knowledge 25
records.content: Federal award standards also emphasize effective internal control and source-supported financial records. 2 CFR 200.303, 2 CFR 200.302

records.title: My recommendation
records.content:
My recommendation
Keep the current formula engine, but reposition it as the first version of the ADRA Recovery
Passport System.
Its promise would be: Enter work once. Explain exceptions once. Recover every eligible cost with a complete evidence trail.
That is simple, memorable, and potentially distinctive. We should describe it as an original ADRA design concept—not claim worldwide uniqueness until a formal patent, product, and academic prior-art search has been completed.

records.title: Master Time Schedule operational capture
records.content: The MTS source captures Date, Employee, Project, Department, Activity Description, optional supporting document, Clock In and Clock Out. Its work table includes progress, total hours, location, comments and document evidence. In the unified system, these fields form the operational evidence record that precedes Recovery Passport assurance.

records.title: Master Time Schedule schedule views and data utilities
records.content: The MTS design provides three schedule views: Time per Individual, Hours per Job and Hours per Month. It also provides search, month/year filtering, pagination, Excel/data export and JSON import. The unified system retains these as operational views while using the workbook Project Master as the authoritative project list.

records.title: Master Time Schedule performance analytics
records.content: The MTS analytics include Top Workers, Daily Analytics with earliest clock-in and latest clock-out, Employee of the Month, Jobs Analytics, Overtime Detection, Department Performance and Project Performance. Worker/department/project weighted performance uses 70% average completion plus 30% normalized hours. These are management analytics only and do not authorize Recovery Passport posting.

records.title: MTS task counter-check at clock-out
records.content: At clock-out the MTS design records percentage completion, whether tasks were completed on time and any communicated delays or challenges. The unified system stores those fields with the completed work session and then creates a DRAFT Recovery Passport time entry; approval remains a separate human control.

records.title: Unified Work-Evidence Spine
records.content: The focal integration point between MTS and Recovery Passport is the work-evidence record. MTS captures what happened in real time; a completed session links to a draft time entry; the workbook engine performs daily reconciliation, eligibility, monthly allocation and Recovery Passport controls; the Agents SDK can reason across both layers and execute supported tasks. Performance scores are never accounting authorization.
